fields.reasoning: Both scripts use their no-milestone change set (Backlog, Orphan) on purpose to test the skip path: daemon-picks.txtar's header says a backlog change set is not started, and its disk-guard and permission-mode checks count exactly one start; daemon-status-projects.txtar (capability daemon-status-across-projects) is about listing each project's skipped change sets with their reason. Setting backlog = "skip" keeps what they test meaningful and exercises the skip value end to end in a real repo, matching how daemon-status-skips already settled daemon-status.txtar (a policy.toml with backlog = "skip"). Rewriting them to expect the backlog pick would drop their only skip-reason coverage across projects and tangle the disk-guard counts with backlog ordering, which the new testscript already covers. The work belongs on daemon-picks-backlog because that leaf changes the default that breaks them.
fields.statement: daemon-picks-backlog also covers the two landed testscripts: cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/daemon-picks.txtar gives its repo a .rhiza/policy.toml with [schedule] backlog = "skip", and cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/daemon-status-projects.txtar gives both projects (repo and second) the same file. Their expectations stay as they are: one 'Started a run of' per poll in daemon-picks.txtar, and each project's Orphan skipped with reason no-milestone / 'serves no milestone' in daemon-status-projects.txtar. The default (after) is tested by daemon-picks-backlog's own new testscript and Go test, not by rewriting these two.
